newsitem.title: UK: Inntrepreneur set for 800 mln stg float - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Inntrepreneur set for 800 mln stg float - analysts.

text.p: Britain's Inntrepreneur Pub Company Ltd, jointly owned by Grand Metropolitan Plc and Australian brewer Foster's Brewing Ltd, is now free to seek a stock market flotation, valuing the company at some 800 million pounds, said analysts.
"These government changes pave the way for a flotation or trade sale of Inntrepreneur," said Panmure Gordon analyst Phillip Shaw.
"It would seem like a reasonable step in the right direction for shareholders," said Merrill Lynch analyst Mark Puleikis.

"We want to get the business and the tenants sorted out and when we have got that sorted out and a thriving business, maybe it will come on the agenda," said Mike Foster, chief executive of Inntrepreneur in an interview. "It's a big animal to make ready for flotation, so if it comes...it will be some way off."

The group, which owns some 2,900 pubs, has property valued at 950 million stg in GrandMet's 1996 report and accounts and showed an operating profit of 58 million stg: a decline of some 30 million stg on 1995 earnings. "For me flotation is an option but it depends on the day which route represents the best value for shareholders," said Foster.

"Its more a part of GrandMet's past than its future. There is no timetable for exiting the business but we have said for some time that it is not core to GrandMet's food and drink operations," said a spokesman for the company.

GrandMet shares closed 2p higher at 460-3/4p, while Scottish & Newcastle shares shed 5-1/2p to 683p. Once a beer supply contract between S&N and Inntrepreneur expires in March 1998, Inntrepreneur tenants will no longer be obliged to sell only S&N ales in their pubs.

But Foster said Inntrepreneur tenants and customers have a strong brand loyalty to S&N beers which meant there was likely to be an outcry if they were removed. -- Tim Farrand, London Newsroom +44 171 542 6437
